title: launcher.json
description: A built app's settings list (dm/launcher.json in an IPA's app, Contents/Resources/dm/launcher.json in a Mac app), written by dm/games/settings.py from dm/games/settings.tsv. docs/frontends.md describes the fields. Schema 1 grows only by optional fields: a reader ignores fields it does not know, and a field keeps its meaning.

schema.description: The list's version; a list without it is schema 1 written before the field existed.

env.description: The environment switch the setting sets.

section.description: The heading it goes under (Game, Resolution, Effects, Frame rate, HDR, Controls and Performance today); sections come in the order of their first rows, and rows in the order to show them. A reader draws a section it does not know like the others, under its name.

note.description: The line under the label; empty for most settings.

default.description: The tested default for this app's platform, with profile defaults resolved.

on.description: toggle: the value the switch takes when on.

off.description: toggle: the value the switch takes when off.

base.description: Render scale only: the 3D views' size the scale multiplies, docked and handheld, from the game's profile; absent for most games.

rate_base.description: A choice whose options are upscale rates (numbers the output is divided by): the output sizes, docked and handheld, from the game's profile, so a front end can show each option's render size in pixels (output / rate, rounded up); when lists other sizes while a setting has a value (<VAR>=<value>), the first that holds wins. Absent for most games.

level.description: basic: a setting a front end shows first. Without it, the front end decides.

needs.description: <VAR>=<value>[|<value>...]: a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> is drawn and has that value (one of the values). A row naming a variable this list does not have stays drawn.

atleast.description: <VAR>: a choice of numbers that cannot go below the number the row that sets <VAR> holds: lower values are not offered, and a lower one held is raised to the lowest offered (a value of that row that is not a number puts no bound). The host refuses or corrects a lower pair as well.

conflicts.description: <VAR>=<value>: the row cannot be used with that value of the row that sets <VAR>: while that row has it, this one is held at its default and drawn disabled, and choosing the value resets this row. <VAR>=<value>:<own>[|<own>...]: only those values of this row: not offered while that row has the value, held at the default, reset when the value is chosen.
